newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Thursday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Thursday:
Spokesman Nikolaus van der Pas said Commissioner Emma Bonino would hold a news conference at 1215/1115 GMT on Friday on humanitarian aid to Albania.

Spokesman Jochen Kubosch briefed on Thursday's Court of Justice judgments. He said the Court had annuled a Commission communication creating an internal market for pension funds. He said the court had judged the communication to be too constraining.

Asked to react to the Court judgment, spokeswoman Elisabetta Olivi said the Commission was unhappy with the decision, but noted the court did not rule against a single market in the pension fund area, only against the procedure the Commission used. Olivi said the Commission is currently working on a green paper expected in May. (See separate story BC-COURT-PENSIONS.)

Spokesman Peter Guilford said a EU delegation, led by Deputy Director General of External Relations Gerard Depeyre, had completed four days consultations in China. He said the talks had for objective to open up China's services market. Guilford said he felt the Chinese were reacting positively to further the talks.

In answer to a question, spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said he was not aware of contacts between Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro and Nigerian Nobel Prize winner Wole Soyinka who was due to visit in Brussels on Thursday.

Asked if Deus Pinheiro would meet the Nigerian Minister invited by the Dutch Presidency to participate to a conference on the future of the Lome Convention to be held in Maastricht in April, Vale de Almeida said that the Commissioner would not be able to meet the 90 ministers expected at the Conference bilaterally and that the Nigerian Minister would not be top of his list.

Spokeswoman Sophie Petzell said the scheme on temporary refugees could not be applied to Italy because it had to be approved by the Justice and Home Affairs Council. She said that would be done "in due time", probably at the 27-28 May Council.
